inputs.sbc_source: SBC verified structurally immaterial: FY2025/H1-2026 StockBasedComp column is 0/blank in the CSV and the H1-2026 note 17 share-based-payment reserve (A$4.65m outstanding options) is overwhelmingly lender/advisor warrants and legacy option grants tied to financing, not an ongoing employee-comp program at this pre-revenue scale. Kept explicit at 0% per section 7(e) (SBC-zero convention), not deleted.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted issued count reconstructed as: 1,404,559,716 ordinary shares on issue at 31-Dec-2025 (H1-2026 interim, note 15 share capital reconciliation) PLUS 73,400,000 shares issued on exercise of unlisted options between 31-Dec-2025 and the interim report date (note 20(b), subsequent events) = 1,477,959,716. Held FLAT for the projection per house convention (SBC is not being expensed as a real economic cost here since it is structurally nil, so there is no double-count risk in holding it flat). NOT included: 209.6m remaining unlisted options (wtd avg strike ~8c, roughly at-the-money vs the A$0.082 ASX price -- modest further dilution risk, noted not modelled) and 36.4m Nebari lender warrants at A$0.2004 strike (~144% out-of-the-money vs spot -- de minimis near-term dilution, noted not modelled). CSV SharesOutstanding column (1,065m-1,076m) is STALE -- it reflects duckdb/core_metrics period-end snapshots that predate the Aug-2025 entitlement offer, Oct/Nov/Dec 2025 placements, and Dec-2025 debt-for-equity conversions documented in the H1-2026 share capital note; this DCF supersedes it with the reconciled H1-2026-plus-subsequent-events count.
inputs.balance_sheet_date: 2025-12-31 (H1-2026 interim, ASX/NZX), with debt anchor rolled forward for the fully-drawn Nebari facility -- see net_debt methodology note below
inputs.net_debt_methodology: Net debt is NOT taken directly off the 31-Dec-2025 balance sheet (A$21.49m) because the capital structure changed materially and knowably between then and the valuation date: the US$30m Nebari Natural Resources Credit Fund II facility -- only US$26m of which was drawn as at the H1-2026 report date -- completed its second and final tranche on 26-Jun-2026, and per H1-2026 notes 14(a)/(b)/(d) this facility (once fully drawn) refinances/absorbs the prior TransAsia senior secured debt, the working-capital facility and the related-party (MCP Manuka Unit Trust) loan that made up most of the 31-Dec-2025 borrowings. The anchor used is: Nebari US$30m fully drawn, converted at spot AUDUSD 0.7115 = A$42.16m total debt, LESS the most recent disclosed cash figure of A$11.1m ('at time of writing', H1-2026 report dated 16-Mar-2026, which also references a further A$9.3m of short-term liquidity not counted here as it is undrawn facility headroom, not cash) = A$31.06m net debt. This is a DOCUMENTED ESTIMATE, not a filed balance sheet figure -- no FY2026 annual or Q4/Q1 quarterly is available yet at the valuation date. It is materially more conservative than using the stale 31-Dec-2025 net debt of A$21.49m, which understates the now-fully-drawn Nebari facility.
inputs.notes: MODEL CHOSEN: Owner-FCF DCF (component build), scenario-weighted, per .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md routing table row 'Operating company, non-US or cyclical' + section 7 adaptations. Manuka is NOT a distressed/receivership shell (still an operating, going, restarting entity with funded restart capital and imminent revenue) and NOT a pure asset play (Taranaki VTM optionality assigned ~zero value per the brief, not driving the valuation) -- so the asset/creditor-waterfall model was NOT used. It is also not yet a normal steady-state producer, so this DCF departs from the reference file's default in one respect: revenue/EBITDA are NOT extrapolated from historical CAGRs (both are meaningless here -- FY2025/H1-2026 revenue is zero, mine was on care & maintenance, and the 5yr equity CAGR of -42% describes a shrinking-to-near-nil pre-restart balance sheet, not a going business). Instead the forward build is a PHYSICAL PRODUCTION RAMP anchored to management's 30-Jan-2026 10-year mine plan (avg EBITDA A$127m p.a., NPV8 A$805m, C1 A$34.4/oz Ag incl. Au credits, restart capex A$26.6m), heavily haircut for: (i) a repeated history of slipped restarts (2022 Wonawinta trial ended early, Mt Boppy halted Q1 2024) and already-revised-up capex (A$18.9m -> A$26.6m); (ii) 39% Inferred-Resource content in the underlying 10.9Mt mine plan (only 6.9Mt/63% is Reserve-backed); (iii) near-record/likely-unsustainable spot gold/silver prices baked into management's own economics; and (iv) explicit going-concern material uncertainty disclosed in the H1-2026 interim (A$21.7m net current liabilities, A$7.7m half-year operating outflow). Base-case mature run-rate EBITDA is set at 40% of management's own 10-year average (A$50.8m vs A$127m); bull at 65% (A$82.6m); bear at 15% (A$19.1m, effectively a struggling-restart case). SBC is genuinely nil (verified) so kept explicit at 0% per section 7(e); no lease-treatment issue (no material IFRS16 lease book disclosed at this scale); no NCI (100% owned across all three assets, stated in Analysis JSON); risk is charged BOTH in the flows (heavy EBITDA haircuts + reserve-life taper + bear-weighted probabilities) AND in a going-concern-loaded WACC of 19% -- this is a deliberate departure from section 7(f)'s 'charge risk once' rule, justified because going-concern/solvency risk (can the company survive to produce at all) is qualitatively different from execution/commodity risk (how much does it produce once it does survive) and the two are not fungible into a single lever; documented here rather than silently stacked. Taranaki VTM: assigned ZERO value in all three scenarios -- the Fast-track application was withdrawn 19-Feb-2026 after a draft decline, this is the SECOND failed NZ marine-consent attempt for this project (after a 2021 Supreme Court-driven refusal), and management has disclosed no alternative pathway or timeline. Any value assigned here would be pure speculation on a NZ regulatory outcome with two prior failures.
inputs.wacc_rationale: WACC of 19% (AUD-denominated, matching the flows currency per section 7(a)) is built as a stack of: AUD risk-free rate ~4.0% (RBA cash rate environment) + equity risk premium ~5.5% (small-cap ASX) + size/micro-cap illiquidity premium ~3.0% (dual-listed ASX-primary/NZX foreign-exempt secondary, thin free float) + single-asset/single-region concentration premium ~2.5% (100% of near-term value depends on one plant restart) + going-concern/financial-distress premium ~4.0% (explicit going-concern material uncertainty disclosed in the H1-2026 interim, high-cost specialist project debt (Nebari), net current liabilities of A.7m). This is a departure from section 7(f) (charge risk once, in the flows OR the discount rate, not both): risk is charged in BOTH the flows (heavy EBITDA haircuts to 15-65% of managements guided average, reserve-life taper, bear-weighted probabilities) AND the discount rate, because solvency/going-concern risk (whether the company survives to produce at all) is treated as qualitatively distinct from execution/commodity risk (how much it produces once it does survive) -- the former is captured in WACC and the probability weights jointly, the latter in the scenario EBITDA/margin/capex haircuts. This dual treatment is a deliberate, documented exception to the usual rule, not an oversight; a reader who prefers strict once-only risk charging should treat the required_return_table at lower rates (9-12%) as the pure-flows-risk-adjusted view.
inputs.fx_note: Financials are AUD (Manuka Resources reports in AUD, dual-listed MKR.AX); MKR.NZ quotes NZD. Converted at AUD/NZD 1.1958, Yahoo AUDNZD=X spot as of 2026-08-20 (inputs.fx_rate_aud_nzd / inputs.fx_as_of). Canonical weighted_iv is NZD to match the quote; weighted_iv_aud is the native basis.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: NONE -- historical CAGRs are not used as a valuation driver
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Historical growth rates are NOT meaningful and are NOT used to drive this valuation. Revenue and FCF CAGRs are undefined/incalculable because FY2025 and H1-2026 revenue is zero (both Mt Boppy and Wonawinta were on care & maintenance) -- the company earned essentially no revenue in the trailing two years. The equity CAGR (-42.5% 5yr, -44.7% 3yr) describes a balance sheet collapsing toward the FY2025 low of A$2.30m book equity BEFORE the Aug-Dec 2025 capital raises that roughly tripled share capital and the subsequent Nebari facility drawdown -- it is a real historical fact but describes a company in run-down/refinancing mode, not the restart economics that actually drive value from here. This DCF instead builds forward FCF as a physical production ramp against management's mine plan (heavily haircut), per inputs.notes.

base.description: Mature run-rate EBITDA = 40% of management's own 10yr average (A$50.8m of A$127m); 3-year production ramp FY27-29; EBITDA margin 42%; modest reserve-life taper from year 8; cash tax rate ramps 0% to 28% (Australian corporate rate) as tax losses are used up

bull.description: Mature run-rate EBITDA = 65% of management's average (A$82.6m); faster 2-year ramp (on-time, on-budget restart); EBITDA margin 48%; taper only from year 9 (better reserve conversion); sustained elevated gold/silver prices

bear.description: Mature run-rate EBITDA = 15% of management's average (A$19.1m) -- restart struggles, desliming circuit underperforms, cost overruns (consistent with the A$18.9m->A$26.6m capex revision already seen), gold/silver prices mean-revert from near-record levels; slower 4-year ramp; equity value floored at zero (limited liability) once net debt is applied -- this scenario represents effective going-concern failure/severe dilution wiping out current equity value, not merely a smaller version of the base case

bear.terminal_pct_of_value_note: not meaningful: enterprise value near zero/negative in this scenario (going-concern failure case)
bear.note: Equity value floored at zero (limited liability). Unfloored DCF equity value is A$-31.33m (negative) -- this scenario models going-concern failure / equity effectively wiped out by dilution and debt claims ranking ahead of shareholders, not merely a weaker production ramp.

entry_price.methodology_note: WACC (19%) EXCEEDS the 15% hurdle rate in this model (unusual -- most tickers in this folder have WACC below 15%). When WACC > hurdle, the house's own risk-adjusted fair value is a HARSHER (lower) number than what a 15%-hurdle investor requires, so the entry price (computed by discounting the same cash flows at the LOWER 15% hurdle rate) comes out ABOVE intrinsic value, not below it. This is the same relationship documented for CDI.NZ in MEMORY.md (17% WACC > 15% hurdle -> entry price above base IV) and is mechanically correct, not an error -- it says a 15%-return investor should be willing to pay MORE than the model's own stacked-risk fair value, because the model's WACC already prices in more risk than a 15% hurdle demands.

base.entry_price_correction_note: Terminal value rebuilt at the hurdle rate 2026-09-01: min(Gordon@hurdle, cap x FCF_N). The superseded value held the WACC-built terminal value and varied only the discounting.

bull.entry_price_correction_note: Terminal value rebuilt at the hurdle rate 2026-09-01: min(Gordon@hurdle, cap x FCF_N). The superseded value held the WACC-built terminal value and varied only the discounting.

bear.note: floored at zero, same going-concern-failure logic as the bear intrinsic value
bear.entry_price_correction_note: Terminal value rebuilt at the hurdle rate 2026-09-01: min(Gordon@hurdle, cap x FCF_N). The superseded value held the WACC-built terminal value and varied only the discounting.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's required return (min(Gordon@r, cap x FCF_N)), so the flows and the exit are charged the same rate. Corrected 2026-09-01.

sensitivity.note: Values in NZD, base scenario. At WACC 15-17% the terminal-growth columns are flat because the 6x terminal-FCF cap (not the Gordon growth formula) binds at those lower discount rates -- see valuation.base.terminal_value_bound.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear weight raised well above the 15% house default to 35% because of (a) explicit going-concern material uncertainty disclosed in the H1-2026 interim financial statements (A$21.7m net current liabilities, A$7.7m half-year operating cash outflow, auditor/director going-concern language), (b) single-asset/single-plant execution risk on an unproven-at-scale desliming circuit retrofit, and (c) a demonstrated history of slipped restarts and upward capex revisions (A$18.9m->A$26.6m) at this company specifically. Bull weight cut to 20% (below the 35% default) because the bull case requires several independent things to go right simultaneously: on-time/on-budget restart, full Inferred-to-Indicated resource conversion, AND sustained near-record gold/silver prices holding through the ramp -- a compound bet, not a single variable. Base gets the residual 45%.
probability_weighted.band_position_note: SBC is verified structurally nil at this pre-revenue restart scale (see inputs.sbc_source) so the house/street band collapses to a single point; band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0%, per section 7(e).

sanity_check.base_case_ev_vs_market_implied_ev: Base-case DCF enterprise value of A$92m compares to a current-price-implied EV of A$152m (market cap A$121m + net debt A$31m) -- the market is pricing in roughly 166% of the haircut-adjusted base case, consistent with a market that is (correctly) discounting a pre-revenue restart with going-concern disclosure heavily, and/or partially pricing bear-case/dilution risk.
sanity_check.management_npv8_aud_805m_vs_house_base_e: Management's own 30-Jan-2026 mine plan states NPV8 of A$805m for the Cobar Basin assets alone (Wonawinta + Mt Boppy, excluding Taranaki VTM). This DCF's base-case enterprise value of A$92m is roughly 11% of that figure -- the gap is the haircut applied for execution risk, Inferred-resource conversion risk, price-assumption fade, and going-concern discount described in inputs.notes. The house view is that management's own number, from an entity with a repeated history of slipped restarts and no revenue in over two years, cannot be taken near face value.

valuation_philosophy: Manuka is a pre-revenue restart-stage junior miner with two mines fully permitted and funded to restart (Nebari facility fully drawn by Jun-2026) but with zero revenue in the trailing two years, explicit going-concern material uncertainty in the latest interim, and a management-published 10-year mine plan (NPV8 A$805m) that is materially unverified given the company's own history of slipped timelines and upward capex revisions. Neither a historical-CAGR extrapolation (meaningless: no revenue to extrapolate) nor a pure asset/creditor waterfall (wrong: this is a going, funded, restarting operation, not a receivership) fits. This DCF instead treats the situation as a PHYSICAL PRODUCTION RAMP scenario problem: three explicit, heavily haircut paths from management's own mine-plan economics to a mature run-rate EBITDA (40% of guidance in base, 65% in bull, 15% in bear), each built up through the standard component chain (EBITDA -> D&A -> tax -> capex -> working capital -> owner FCF), discounted at a going-concern-loaded 19% WACC, terminal-valued at the LOWER of Gordon growth or a conservative 6x terminal-FCF cap (appropriate for a reserve-depleting single-asset miner, not a perpetual compounder), and probability-weighted 35/45/20 bear/base/bull -- bear weighted up from the 15% house default specifically for the disclosed going-concern risk. The Taranaki VTM iron-sands project is assigned zero value in every scenario: its Fast-track consent application was withdrawn in Feb-2026 after a draft decline, the second such failure for this project, with no disclosed alternative pathway. The resulting weighted intrinsic value of NZ$0.0536 (upside -43.6% to the NZ$0.095 quote) and base-case value of NZ$0.0491 both sit below the current market price, indicating the market is ascribing more optimism to a successful, on-time, on-budget, on-plan restart than this model's haircuts allow -- consistent with elevated, possibly re-rating-driven, gold/silver-sector sentiment rather than fully de-risked mine-plan economics.
